author: NorthEast News Desk
body: JetBlue Airways raised its third-quarter unit-revenue forecast Thursday, pointing to steady travel demand even as higher fuel prices and operational disruptions increased the carrier’s expected costs.

The New York-based airline now projects revenue per available seat mile to rise 17% to 20% from a year earlier, up from its previous range of 12.5% to 16.5%. That is a forward-looking company estimate, not a completed quarterly result.

Cost pressure moved in the same direction. JetBlue increased its expected average fuel price to $3.96 per gallon from $3.49. It also projected nonfuel unit costs to rise 6% to 8%, compared with an earlier 2.5% to 4.5% range, after weather and air-traffic-control disruptions increased cancellations during July and August.

JetBlue cut its capacity-growth forecast to 1.5% to 3.5% from 3% to 6%. The revisions give investors a mixed picture: stronger revenue for each unit of flying, but fewer planned seats and a higher expense base. The ultimate margin effect will depend on realized fares, fuel prices and operations through the quarter’s end.
dek: The New York-based airline lifted its third-quarter unit-revenue forecast but cut capacity growth and projected higher fuel and nonfuel expenses.
headline: JetBlue raises seat-revenue outlook as fuel and disruption costs climb
